in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're very welcome – I'm happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To continue, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, does he live with you, or do you pay towards his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. I'm responsible for taking care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me: are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I have a few follow-up questions to understand your situation better.

Could you tell me which country you are currently living in, and what is the reason for being abroad? For example, are you working, or is it for another reason?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all the specific details about where exactly I am and why - I just want to know if I can still claim Child Benefit for Alex even though we're not in the UK right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand, and I appreciate your privacy. However, to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit while living abroad, I do need to ask a few general questions – I'll keep them as straightforward as possible.

Could you tell me: are you or your partner (if you have one) currently employed by or working for the UK government, or are you a member of the UK armed forces serving overseas?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us work for the UK government or are in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

One more important question: are you or your partner currently paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or are you employed by a company that is based in the UK (even though you are living abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, and we don't work for a UK-based company.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me summarise:

- Alex is 6 years old and lives with you
- You are responsible for his care
- You are currently living abroad (outside the UK)
- Neither you nor your partner work for the UK government or are in the UK armed forces
- Neither of you are paying UK National Insurance contributions or working for a UK-based company

I'll now provide my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

While Alex is within the eligible age range (under 16) and you are responsible for his care, Child Benefit generally requires the claimant to be living in the United Kingdom. There are some exceptions that allow people living abroad to still claim, including:

- Working for the UK government abroad (Crown servants)
- Serving in the UK armed forces overseas
- Working abroad while still paying UK National Insurance contributions
- Working for a UK-based employer while abroad

Since you've confirmed that none of these circumstances apply to your situation, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK.

**What you can do:**

If your circumstances change in the future – for example, if you return to live in the UK – you may become eligible at that point and could make a claim then.

I hope this information is helpful, and I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
